description:
Worktree detection and primary-checkout discovery answer from one primitive instead of five
independent implementations.

## Background

Five separate implementations currently decide whether the current checkout is a linked
non-primary worktree and where the primary checkout lives: a version-control layout probe
computed before every dispatch, a test for whether the repository pointer is a file in the
JSON storage backend, a library-level path comparison in index loading, an inline
version-control invocation in issue loading, and a linked-checkout fallback in the
repository-state store. They can disagree, and nothing names one of them as authoritative.
The layout probe is the most complete and is already computed before dispatch, so it becomes
the single answer.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: One primitive answers whether the selected data root sits inside a linked non-primary checkout and where the primary checkout's store is; no second implementation of either question survives in storage or command code.
- [hard] REQ-02: Outside version control the primitive reports a non-linked checkout rather than failing, so repositories without version control keep working.
- [hard] REQ-03: When an environment override selects the data root, classification follows that selected root's location rather than the process working directory, and that behaviour is covered.
- [hard] REQ-04: The layered issue read fallback, the deletion policy, and worktree introspection keep their current observable behaviour while reading the converged primitive.

## Notes

The read-side layered issue resolution (local store, then version-control history, then the
primary checkout) is documented adopter-facing behaviour and is unchanged here; only the
detection question underneath it converges.
title: Converge worktree detection on one primitive
